extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners (primary) and patent applicants/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance on entry, disapproval, and treatment of preliminary and supplemental amendments and replies to non-final and final Office actions (37 CFR 1.111, 1.115, 1.121, 1.135). Covers timing limits, grounds for denial, examiner procedures, form paragraphs, and applicant obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of all claims without substitute claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment seeking cancellation of all the claims without presenting any new or substitute claims will be disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not enter such an amendment. The application will not be denied a filing date merely because such a preliminary amendment was submitted on filing. For fee calculation purposes, the Office will treat such an application as containing only a single claim. In most cases such an amendment would not meet 37 CFR 1.121(c) requiring a complete claim listing; the Office will send a notice of non-compliant amendment and require an amendment in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121. (See Exxon Corp. v. Phillips Petroleum Co.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment may be disapproved if it unduly interferes with first Office action preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment may be disapproved if the preliminary amendment unduly interferes with the preparation of a first Office action. Factors considered include the state of preparation of a first Office action as of the date of receipt (37 CFR 1.6) and the nature of any changes to the specification or claims that would result from entry of the preliminary amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to file preliminary amendments as soon as possible. If the examiner has already begun significant preparation (search/draft) before receipt, and entry would require significant additional time, entry may be denied (SPE approval required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor timing for preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment will not be disapproved under the 'unduly interferes' rule if it is filed no later than certain time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These acceptable filing time limits are: (i) three months from the filing date of an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b); (ii) the filing date of a continued prosecution application under 37 CFR 1.53(d); or (iii) three months from the date the national stage is entered per 37 CFR 1.491 for an international application. These time periods are not extendable (37 CFR 1.115(b)(3)-(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-condition test for denying entry after safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: If a preliminary amendment is filed after the safe-harbor time periods, entry may be denied only if two conditions are met: (A) the examiner has devoted a significant amount of time preparing a first Office action before the amendment's receipt date; and (B) entry of the amendment would require significant additional time in preparing the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of changes that would satisfy condition (B) include: amends the claims; adds numerous new claims; amends the specification to change the scope of the claims; amends the specification raising a new matter issue; includes arguments; includes an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 or 1.132; includes evidence traversing rejections from a prior Office action. This list is not exhaustive. If the two conditions are met, the examiner should obtain SPE approval before denying entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: When disapproval is inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Denying entry of a preliminary amendment is inappropriate if either the examiner has NOT devoted significant time in preparing an Office action before receipt, or the entry would NOT require significant additional time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples where entry should not be denied include: amendment merely cancels some pending claims; amends claims to overcome rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph; amends claims to place the application in condition for allowance; includes only changes previously suggested by the examiner and would not require significant additional time. If the examiner has only inspected the file for formal requirements and not started substantive work, the amendment should be entered and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.46 use and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.46 should be used to notify applicant that the entry of a preliminary amendment is denied because the amendment unduly interferes with preparation of an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paragraph must state the date of receipt (37 CFR 1.6), describe state of preparation (e.g., claim analysis/search/draft status), and explain specifically how entry would require significant additional time (e.g., conduct prior art search in another classification, revise Office action extensively). Include warning about timely filing a responsive reply to avoid abandonment and suggest resubmitting the amendment with a responsive reply if not final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for fully responsive reply (37 CFR 1.111(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, the applicant must reply to the Office action. The reply must be reduced to writing which distinctly and specifically points out the supposed errors in the examiner’s action and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must present arguments pointing out the specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references. A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specifics does not comply. The reply must appear to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application or reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reply must point out patentable novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending in reply to a rejection, the applicant must clearly point out the patentable novelty believed to be present in view of the cited art or objections and show how the amendments avoid those references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a reply to a requirement is necessary for further consideration or allowable subject matter has been indicated, a complete reply must comply with formal requirements or specifically traverse each formal requirement not complied with. Support for amendments to the disclosure should be specifically pointed out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between formal matters and merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing and specification corrections, presentation of a new oath, etc., are generally formal matters, but the line between formal matters and those touching the merits is not sharp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of the merits may require insisting upon such corrections or new oath prior to any indication of allowable subject matter. Filing of drawing corrections in reply to an objection to the drawings cannot normally be held in abeyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after subsequent non-final actions increasing claim count
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment submitted after a second or subsequent non-final action which is otherwise responsive but increases the number of claims drawn to the invention previously acted upon is not to be held not fully responsive for that reason alone (see 37 CFR 1.112).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments increasing claim count should not automatically be treated as non-responsive merely because they add claims; consider overall responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment options for amendments not fully responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may treat an amendment not fully responsive to a non-final Office action by: (A) accepting the amendment as an adequate reply to avoid abandonment; (B) notifying the applicant that the reply must be completed within the remaining period for reply (or extension) to avoid abandonment; or (C) setting a new time period for applicant to complete the reply pursuant to 37 CFR 1.135(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The choice depends on whether the amendment is bona fide, whether there is sufficient time remaining for applicant’s reply, and the nature of the deficiency. If serious deficiency (unsigned or not filed in reply), do not further examine on the merits until omission is timely supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor vs. serious deficiencies in replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment substantially responds but contains a minor deficiency (e.g., fails to treat every rejection), the examiner may act on the amendment and issue a new office action reiterating what remains. For serious deficiencies, the examiner should notify applicant to supply omission within remaining time or set a 1-month time period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) if insufficient time remains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new time period is set under 1.135(c), applicant must supply the omission within that period (or file a continuing application). The examiner should not further examine the merits unless the omission is timely supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.135(c) applies only to inadvertent omissions in bona fide replies
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.135(c) authorizes giving a new time period to supply an omission when the reply is a bona fide attempt to advance the application but inadvertently omitted some matter or compliance; deliberate omissions are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If omission was deliberate (e.g., refusing to elect species because applicant believes requirement improper), the amendment is not a bona fide attempt and examiner has no authority to postpone abandonment decision. Once inadvertence is brought to applicant's attention, inadvertence no longer exists and a second 1-month time is not appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion to refuse 1.135(c) relief if abuse suspected
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.135(c) authorizes but does not require an examiner to give additional time; examiner may refuse to grant additional time if the applicant is attempting to abuse the practice to obtain more time or if there is sufficient time remaining to file a reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where refusal is appropriate, the examiner should indicate by telephone or Office communication that the reply must be completed within the period for reply or extension to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No 1.135(c) relief after final Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice under 37 CFR 1.135(c) of giving a time period to supply an omission does not apply after a final Office action. Amendments after final are approved for entry only if they place the application in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment after final does not place the application in condition for allowance, it should be denied entry. Applicant may obtain additional time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) to file another or supplemental amendment to supply the omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendment and withdrawal of finality (discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply to a final Office action substantially places the application in condition for allowance, an examiner may request applicant authorize an examiner's amendment to correct an omission and place the application in condition for allowance; the date of reply is date of such authorization. Examiner may also enter the reply, withdraw finality, and issue a new Office action or other appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These actions are solely within the examiner's discretion and may include issuing a non-final or final Office action or closing prosecution on the merits in an otherwise allowable application (Ex parte Quayle authority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies: limits and entry conditions (37 CFR 1.111(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply that is supplemental to a reply in compliance with 37 CFR 1.111(b) will not be entered as a matter of right except as provided. The Office may enter a supplemental reply if it is clearly limited to cancellation of a claim(s); adoption of the examiner suggestion(s); placement of the application in condition for allowance; reply to an Office requirement made after the first reply was filed; correction of informalities (e.g., typographical errors); or simplification of issues for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental reply will be entered if filed within a period during which action by the Office is suspended under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c). If a supplemental reply is not approved for entry, the examiner should notify applicant in the subsequent Office action and applicant should include desired changes in the reply to the next Office action. Submission of a supplemental reply may reduce accumulated patent term adjustment under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(8). Use form paragraph 7.147 to notify applicant when supplemental reply is not entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reply received after Office action mail date is not serviced
rubrics_metrics.description: If a supplemental reply is received after the mail date of an Office action and it is not responsive to that Office action, the Office will not mail a new Office action responsive to that supplemental reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a courtesy, applicant may be notified that the supplemental reply is nonresponsive and that a timely responsive reply must be filed to avoid abandonment. If applicant wants the non-entered supplemental reply considered, include the changes in the reply to the next Office action; simply requesting entry later is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims presented without pointing out patentable novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims presented in an amendment with no attempt to point out the patentable novelty should not be allowed; such an amendment may be held not fully responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claims as amended are clearly open to rejection on the record, a final rejection should generally be made. If statutory reply period has expired or nearly expired, set time to furnish proper reply per MPEP § 714.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate inspection checklist for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions by applicant, especially filed near end of reply period, should be inspected immediately upon filing to determine whether they are completely responsive to the preceding Office action to prevent abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should inspect whether: amendment is properly signed (MPEP § 714.01(a)); filed within statutory/shortened time limits; fully responsive and complies with 37 CFR 1.121; changes warrant transfer; application is special; claims for interference have been copied; traversal of a restriction requirement exists; amendment prepared on non-permanent paper; applicant has cited references; terminal disclaimer filed; any security-related matter added. Prompt supplemental action may be needed if amendment crosses with the mailed action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not in permanent ink (37 CFR 1.52(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(a) requires 'permanent dark ink or its equivalent' for papers that become part of the record; 'easily erasable' paper violates the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If nonpermanent medium is used, applicant should be promptly notified that the amendment is not entered and required to file a permanent copy within one month or order a copy to be made by the PTO at applicant's expense; physical entry is made from the permanent copy. If no appropriate reply, PTO will make a copy and charge applicant. A good photocopy or facsimile on satisfactory paper is acceptable in many cases; see MPEP § 608.01 for acceptable copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is required to pay excess claims fees for claims in excess of statutorily allowed counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated: fees are required for each claim that is in excess of 3 in independent form or in excess of 20 total claims (whether dependent or independent). (Text truncated in chunk but rule is indicated.) See MPEP §§ on fees for full details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.95/7.95.01 for bona fide but non-responsive amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.95 to notify applicant that a reply appears bona fide but is not fully responsive and grant a one month (or 30 days) time period to supply omissions to avoid abandonment. Use 7.95.01 to notify lack of arguments when appropriate (primarily pro se).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 7.95 must specify omissions and give the TIME PERIOD of ONE (1) MONTH or THIRTY (30) DAYS from mailing date within which to supply omissions; extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a). 7.95.01 should be preceded by 7.95 and requests submission of arguments under 'Remarks' discussing references and how claims avoid them.
